assign.step: read parent/sibling requirements + Assistant.js/assistant.md + engine.js/structure.js + prompt-relay/reply-relay hooks + sessions.mjs

decision.question: what signal tells the hooks 'this is the owner's own interactive session, not a minion/mastermind' — the brief suggested reusing prompt-relay.mjs's author:"owner" field
decision.why: reply-relay.mjs's own doc comment already found, by testing on itself, that author:"owner" is stamped for EVERY session including a Servex-spawned minion's first prompt (its whole brief arrives as an ordinary UserPromptSubmit) — so that field cannot tell owner-interactive apart from minion/mastermind. SERVEX_MCP is only ever set on a process Servex itself spawned, so its absence is the correct, already-proven test. Used in both prompt-relay.mjs and reply-relay.mjs now, consistently.

decision.question: what should the position notice to Servex actually point at, for the Stop hook's reply
options: transcript_path + the assistant message's own index inside Claude Code's raw transcript jsonl (the brief's literal suggestion)
file + line inside .claude/prompts/<date>.jsonl — the SAME simple pointer shape as the prompt side, into the text reply-relay.mjs had already extracted and written
decision.why: reply-relay.mjs already does the hard part (finding the last real assistant text block, skipping sidechains and tool-only turns) and writes a clean one-line record. Pointing Servex at Claude Code's OWN raw transcript format instead would mean Echo.js has to re-implement that same extraction a second time (law 6), just to end up reading the exact same text reply-relay.mjs already wrote cleanly to .claude/prompts/. The brief's own wording left this open ("transcript_path + message index, or similar — your call").

assign.step: build Servex/agents/Echo.js + echo.md: per-session echo role, step-by-step refine_step tool

decision.question: 5-step write order: clean, references, sections, asks_flags, done -- but sections is computed mechanically before the model is even sent anything
options: write sections immediately after clean, both code-authored, before the model's first tool call
hold sections back and write it right after the model's 'references' call lands, matching the owner's own literal stated order
decision.chose: hold it back, write right after references
decision.why: found the owner's own exact stated step order inside session 361c4d18's own transcript (reply at 2026-10-03T02:21, heading "Big text moves by hook, never through a tool call"): "clean -> names and references -> sections -> asks and flags -> done". sections is still 100% code-computed (never a model tool call), only the ORDER it lands on disk in was moved to match what the owner actually said, per law 4.

decision.question: what model does clean() use for echo's live calls
options: clean()'s own default (minion-core's litmus picked haiku as cheapest)
decision.why: task-mastermind-prompt-refine's own call, relayed mid-task: haiku took 123s/call vs deepseek's 8s in minion-core's own litmus run (Server/refine-litmus-result.json), both passed the mechanical check -- a 15x latency win matters far more than the ~22-cent gap on a path meant to be watched live.

decision.question: how should an echo agent answer, given the owner's amendment to write step by step through tool calls
options: one append_refined call carrying the whole nested record
a new refine_step tool, one call per step (clean, references, sections, asks_flags, done)
decision.chose: new refine_step tool, step by step
decision.why: the owner's own amendment (vscode-mastermind, 2026-10-02) said this explicitly, and the brief's own wording allowed either extending append_prompt_event or adding a new tool; a new tool keeps Assistant.js's own door untouched (it answers a different log, prompts, not echo) and keeps the schema honest about what each step actually carries.

decision.question: what does 'resolves' (a reply answering an earlier flag) carry
options: an array of {flag_from_at, note} objects, matching the original brief's own sketch
a single re (the earlier prompt's own at) + a single resolves string, one call per resolved flag
decision.why: simpler, and the model already has re on the tool call's own schema for exactly this; one call per resolved flag is fine since this only ever fires rarely (a reply plainly answering an old question).
